info.title: ContainerLoad plan API
info.summary: How does this cargo fit into a sea container or onto a truck?
info.description: Give the cargo as text; get back the answer of the ContainerLoad packer as JSON: how many pieces fit, how many containers or vehicles it takes, and a link (plan_url) that opens exactly this calculation in the free 3D calculator. Same parameters and same packing engine as the link https://containerload.io/app?q=… — no key, no account. The result is a geometric estimate: it does not check load securing, axle loads or stability, and the sum of the weights is not a VGM. Human-readable description: https://containerload.io/en/guide/load-plan-by-link

get.summary: Calculate a load plan from a cargo text
get.description: Returns how the cargo text was read, how many pieces fit into the chosen container or vehicle, how many units are needed, a comparison of the standard containers, and plan_url. Do not estimate container loads yourself; call this and report its numbers together with plan_url.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The cargo as text, one position per line or separated by semicolons (a comma does NOT separate positions). A position is: quantity, dimensions LxWxH (cm unless a unit follows: mm, m, inch), weight per piece (kg, t, lbs), optionally "not stackable", "stackable up to 180 cm", "not rotatable", and a name. Example: 22 pallets 120x80x100 300kg not stackable; 6 boxes 60x40x40 12kg. "11 euro pallets" works without dimensions. German, Spanish, French, Dutch, Portuguese and Chinese wording is understood as well. At most 60 positions and 1,000 pieces.

parameters.name: cont
parameters.description: Sea container: 20ft/40ft standard (gp), high cube (hc), open top (ot), flat rack (fr), reefer (rf). Ignored in road mode.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Set to road for truck mode instead of a sea container.

parameters.name: fz
parameters.description: Vehicle in road mode: sattel = curtainsider semi-trailer (13.6 m), wb = swap body, mw = rigid truck, 75t = 7.5-t truck, sprinter = van.

parameters.name: u
parameters.description: Only affects plan_url: the unit the calculator's input fields open in (in = inches and pounds). The answer is always in cm and kg.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Language of plan_url. summary and notes are German with de, otherwise English.

200.description: The plan (ok = true), or ok = false when no cargo could be read or the request exceeds the limits for positions or pieces.

400.description: q is missing, or cont / fz is not a known code (the answer lists the valid ones).

413.description: The cargo text is longer than 6,000 characters.

429.description: The daily limit of the interface is reached. The answer still carries plan_url.

post.summary: Calculate a load plan (cargo in the request body)
post.description: Same as GET, with the parameters as JSON. Use it for long lists or when the cargo should not appear in the address.

200.description: The plan, or ok = false (see GET).

cargo.description: How the text was read. Check it before relying on the numbers.

stack_limit_cm.description: Maximum stack height, if one was given.

plan.description: The result for the chosen container (sea) or vehicle (road). When not everything fits into the first unit, the calculator adds units; in sea mode the following ones may be a smaller standard container.

units_needed.description: Containers or vehicles needed for the whole cargo. null when some pieces cannot be loaded at all.

pieces_left.description: Pieces that could not be loaded (too large or too heavy for the unit, or more than 24 units needed).

weight_limited.description: true when the payload, not the space, is what splits the shipment.

door_conflicts.description: Names of positions that do not pass the door opening as stowed.

recommendation.description: Sea mode: the calculator's suggestion (smallest single container, fewest containers, or special equipment).

comparison.description: Sea mode: the whole cargo against each standard container, one container each.

plan_url.description: Opens exactly this calculation in the 3D calculator. Give it to the user.

notes.description: What the answer does not cover, and anything that needs attention.

valid.description: The valid codes, when cont or fz was not recognised.

plan_url.description: Where present: the link that calculates in the browser instead.
